terms.definition: Energy can be transferred usefully, stored or dissipated, but cannot be created or destroyed.
terms.examiner: The total energy is the same before and after.

terms.definition: Energy transferred to the surroundings in a way that is not useful; often described as wasted.
Useful output energy transfer ÷ total input energy transfer; or useful power output ÷ total power input.
terms.examiner: No unit, or ×100 for a percentage. Never more than 100%.

terms.definition: Lubrication reduces friction; thermal insulation reduces heating of the surroundings.
terms.examiner: Thicker walls with lower thermal conductivity lose energy more slowly.

terms.definition: How well a material conducts energy by heating; the higher it is, the faster the energy transfer.
terms.examiner: Separate Physics required practical on insulation.
